identification_strategy: One-line: EVENT_STUDY — treatment = households experiencing a health shock in year τ, control = households experiencing the same shock but in year τ + Δ; shock/instrument/cutoff = severe health shocks (nonfatal heart attacks and strokes)

key_variables.treatment: households experiencing a health shock in year τ
key_variables.control: households experiencing the same shock but in year τ + Δ
key_variables.outcome: consumption of preventive care and health-related behaviors
key_variables.instrument_or_cutoff: severe health shocks (nonfatal heart attacks and strokes)

conclusion_detail: Spouses and adult children immediately improve their health behaviors in response to health shocks, with effects being significant and persistent.
main_effect: 15% increase among prime-age spouses, 37% and 16% increases among younger and older adult children respectively
key_robustness: alternative control group matching on pre-shock risk factors
notes: The study uses a quasi-experimental design with potential randomness in shock timing, but there may still be unobserved factors affecting the results.
